dataset.description:
This description covers the data management approach for research data generated within this project under the LCS FARP framework.
The project involves experimental spectroscopy, computational analysis, and machine learning-based processing of atomic and molecular data. The purpose of this description is to define how research data will be documented, managed, stored, secured, and shared in accordance with FAIR principles and Latvian Council of Science requirements.

distribution.title:
The purpose of data collection and generation in this project is to create comprehensive experimental and computational datasets for the analysis of atomic and molecular structures using high-resolution spectroscopy and machine learning methods.
Experimental data will be generated through laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) and Fourier-transform (FT) spectroscopy measurements, producing high-resolution spectral information under controlled laboratory conditions. These datasets will be used to identify spectral features, classify emission lines, support the discovery of unknown transitions, and improve the understanding of atomic structures such as fine structure, hyperfine structure, and isotop shifts.
Additional derived data will be generated through preprocessing, feature extraction, and machine learning analysis pipelines. The collected and generated data directly support the project’s objective of developing an automated framework for spectroscopy data acquisition, analysis, and interpretation, enabling more efficient and reproducible research workflows.

dataset.title: LCS FARP Data Management Description

dmp.description:
This Data Management Plan (DMP) describes the management of data generated within the project focused on automated high-resolution spectroscopy and machine learning for atomic and molecular data analysis.
The project will generate experimental and computational research data, including spectroscopy measurements obtained through laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) and Fourier-transform (FT) spectroscopy, as well as derived datasets such as processed spectral data and machine learning analysis outputs.
The purpose of this DMP is to define a structured approach for handling the full data lifecycle, including acquisition, processing, storage, documentation, security, and long-term preservation. Particular attention is given to data quality, traceability, reproducibility, and effective internal research data management.
Where appropriate, selected research outputs such as software tools, algorithms, and publication-supporting materials may be shared. Primary experimental datasets will be managed in accordance with institutional research data management practices and project-specific access restrictions.
